query: Deadline Night Deadline night. The front page fell through at nine and Nessa is pacing. "We need eight hundred words by four," she says. "Anybody with a quill that writes fast, now is the time." Sit it out with the quill You and the quill write until four. By the end it finishes your sentences only when you want it to. You are both too tired to argue. Nessa puts your name on the page, small. Go to bed You sleep. In the morning the front page is late and Nessa is hoarse, and the quill has written a bitter little poem about you on the pillowcase.

results.title: The Editor Sleeps
results.excerpt:
The Editor Sleeps
Nessa hasn't slept properly in a week. She's asleep at her desk now, and her quill — unsupervised — is still writing next week's paper. It has started inventing news.
Put her to bed and run the paper yourself
You edit, typeset and print one issue, and miss a day
